review_method: Visual inspection of every second decoded frame across the entire MP4 plus native-resolution transition frames, followed by native initial PNG
initial_scene: Middle third-person view only: an orange mat on a gray table, an empty white bowl at upper left, an orange carrot with green leaves near the center, a yellow ridged fruit-shaped object to its right, and a dark curved fruit-shaped object with a green stem at upper right. A green cucumber-shaped object and three rounded orange/pink/yellow objects form a cluster at lower left. The active white-and-blue arm and open two-finger gripper are at the rear; a second arm remains in the lower-left foreground. Black curtain behind the table.

observed_sequence.action: Initial stationary scene; active gripper open above the rear tabletop, white bowl empty and all objects on the mat.
Active arm approaches the orange carrot, straddles it, and closes the gripper around its narrower orange end. Native frame 288 shows closure while carrot remains on the mat.
Arm lifts and carries the carrot over the white bowl; the green leafy end hangs free. Carrot is still held at frame 345.

Carrot releases at approximately frame 346 and settles fully inside the white bowl by frame 350. The empty gripper remains briefly above it, then withdraws to the rear by about frame 395. Carrot remains in the bowl through frame 399.

Following a brief stationary rear pose, the empty gripper moves down over the now-empty central tabletop, closes there without picking up any object, then lifts back. No object transfers in this extra cycle.

Arm approaches and grasps the yellow ridged fruit-shaped object, lifts it, and moves toward the bowl; frame 700 shows it suspended to the right of the bowl. Around frames 703-706 it slips/drops onto the mat outside the bowl.
Yellow object bounces/rolls and settles on the mat to the right of the bowl; empty gripper continues above the bowl and withdraws without having delivered the object.
Arm returns to the displaced yellow object and closes on it but lifts empty; object stays on the mat, slightly shifted. Native frames 862 and 888 distinguish the failed grasp and empty withdrawal.

Arm retries the yellow object, grasps it successfully, and carries it to the bowl. While held over/against the bowl rim, bowl shifts right; a human hand enters from the right around frame 1084 and repositions/supports the bowl near the gripper.

Yellow object releases into the white bowl by frame 1096. A human hand continues repositioning and briefly tilting the bowl; carrot and yellow object remain inside. Bowl returns to upper-left area by about frame 1136.
Arm attempts to grasp the dark curved fruit-shaped object at upper right, shifts it slightly but lifts empty. The empty arm goes to the bowl and withdraws while dark object remains on the mat.
Arm retries the dark curved fruit-shaped object, closes around it, and successfully lifts it by frame 1460. It transfers the object over the bowl, lowers, and releases it inside by about frame 1532.
Empty gripper retracts and stops above rear tabletop. White bowl contains carrot, yellow ridged object, and dark curved object; original cluster at lower left remains untouched.

selected_segment.reason: Retains the first complete independent manipulation: carrot approach, grasp, lift, transfer, release, settling and withdrawal. Native frames 345-350 establish release/settling, and 395-400 show an empty withdrawn gripper with the carrot stably inside the bowl. Ends before the subsequent empty-tabletop gripper cycle and later yellow-object attempts.
selected_segment.terminal_state: Orange carrot rests entirely inside the white bowl; active gripper has withdrawn empty to the rear. All other objects remain on the mat.
